predecessors.name: Denmark-Norway
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Norway that Denmark 'was forced by the Treaty of Kiel to cede ... to Sweden' in 1814 (Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands stayed Danish)

ledger.x: 1814: Norway rises as a kingdom of its own.
14 August 1814: the Convention of Moss ends the two-week war with 'a general cease-fire'; Norway was not recognized as having accepted the Treaty of Kiel.
4 November 1814: Norway enters the union with Sweden.
ledger.cpn: United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway

ledger.x: 7 June 1905: the Storting unanimously declares the union with Sweden dissolved.
ledger.cpn: United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway

ledger.x: 18 November 1905: Prince Carl of Denmark accepts the Norwegian throne as Haakon VII (the Union page's lead gives 18 November; its body says he arrived in Norway on 25 November), ending the Swedish-Norwegian crown.
1922: Norway annexes the middle of Jan Mayen.
June-July 1931: Norway lays claim to Erik the Red's Land.
5 April 1933: the Permanent Court of International Justice rules for Denmark ('Territory awarded to Denmark: 5 April 1933'); 'Norway lost and after the ruling it abandoned its claim'.
1940: the king and government go to London.
9 April 1940: Germany invades Norway (Operation Weserübung); the occupation 'began on 9 April 1940'.
10 June 1940: 'Conventional armed resistance to the German invasion ended on 10 June 1940'; the Norwegian 6th Division surrendered in Northern Norway that day.

June 1940: the German occupation of the mainland is complete; Reichskommissar Josef Terboven took over power by forming his own cabinet on 20 September 1940 and Quisling was 're-instituted as head of state on 20 February 1942' of a 'pro-German puppet government'.

8 May 1945: 'Nazi Germany controlled Norway until the capitulation of German forces in Europe on 8 May 1945'; an Allied military mission arrived in Oslo to deliver the conditions and the surrender took effect at midnight.
7 June 1945: King Haakon VII and the royal family arrive in Oslo and General Sir Andrew Thorne transfers power to the King that day; the government returns from London.

wars.name: Swedish-Norwegian War (1814)
wars.outcome: A two-week war: the Swedes took Hvaler on 27 July, the Convention of Moss (14 August) gave 'a general cease-fire' and Christian Frederick abdicated on 10 October; the Storting accepted the union with Sweden on 4 November.

wars.name: Erik the Red's Land
wars.outcome: No fighting: Norway proclaimed the strip Norwegian on 10 July 1931 and the Permanent Court of International Justice awarded it to Denmark on 5 April 1933; Norway abandoned the claim.

wars.name: Norwegian campaign
wars.outcome: Germany invaded on 9 April 1940; 'conventional armed resistance ... ended on 10 June 1940' and the mainland was occupied until 8 May 1945.

certainty.note: A kingdom with an old settled land frontier; the pages opened give no surveyed line (the 1905 Karlstad neutral zone is the only frontier text); the Union page does not describe the extent.
Svalbard is defined by the 1920 treaty (in force 1925) and Jan Mayen by the 1930 act; the Greenland strip of 1931-1933 was only claimed and is soft.
Treaty and statutory limits; during 1940-1945 the mainland frontier is unchanged under occupation.
